channel.title: Molecular & Cell Biology Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Nature Cell Biology, Genome Biology, Genome Research, and Molecular Cell.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Rapid customization of base editors via machine learning-powered combinatorial mutagenesis
item.description: Peng et al. leverage artificial intelligence tools to efficiently explore the vast mutational space, screening base-editor variants in human cells with minimal experimental data. Their approach yields YC motif-specific cytosine base editors that are efficient in reducing bystander and other unwanted edits.

item.title: Molecular Cell: MRE11 proximal polyadenylation site-mediated looping impacts transcription and genomic stability
item.description: Huang et al. demonstrate that a proximal polyadenylation site in MRE11 forms a promoter-PAS loop that supports RNA polymerase recycling and transcription. Disruption reduces MRN expression, impairs checkpoint function, and induces aberrant DNA replication, revealing PAS-mediated chromatin looping as a mechanism linking transcriptional regulation to genome stability.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Cytoplasmic RNase III Drosha controls lipogenesis by noncanonical regulation of SREBP1
item.description: Nie et al. identify a noncanonical function of Drosha beyond its role in miRNA biogenesis. They report that Drosha promotes SREBP1 maturation and lipogenesis by facilitating COPII assembly, which is independent of the RNase activity of Drosha required for miRNA biogenesis. These findings advance our understanding of the multifaceted roles of Drosha.

item.title: Molecular Cell: The discovery of 5mC-selective deaminases and their application to ultra-sensitive direct sequencing of methylated sites at base resolution
item.description: Our study describes the discovery of virally encoded cytidine deaminases that specifically convert 5mC to T. This activity enables direct and simultaneous methylome and genome sequencing.

item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 13 April 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01928-6 Paquola et al. present a technique named lipid-trap mass spectrometry (LTMS) to study lipid–protein interactions directly captured from mammalian cells.

item.title: Molecular Cell: H2AK119ub1-MLL2 counteraction underlies heritable H3K27me3 formation in oocytes
item.description: Mei et al. reveal that the Polycomb mark H2AK119ub1 maintains gene silencing in mouse oocytes by opposing MLL2 activity, enabling the establishment of heritable H3K27me3. They uncover how the balance between repressive and activating chromatin mechanisms shapes the maternal epigenome.

item.title: Genome Biology: DNA damaging properties of G-quadruplex ligand QN-302 are potentiated by the DNA repair inhibitor Olaparib and mitigated by the molecular helicase PhpC
Genome Biology: Long-read sequencing identifies aberrant fragmentation patterns linked to elevated cell-free DNA levels in cancer
Molecular Cell: Condition-dependent amorphous protein agglomerates control cytoplasmic rheology
item.description: Losa et al. show that nutrient-dependent changes in E. coli cytoplasmic rheology arise from amorphous agglomerates formed by self-association of amino acid metabolic enzymes. These agglomerates slow down macromolecular diffusion and increase cytoplasmic elasticity, revealing metabolic remodeling as a regulator of intracellular transport and organization.

item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 08 April 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01909-9 This Perspective proposes the use of an integrative embedded ethics approach to evaluate human stem-cell-based embryo models and outlines a nested benchmarking strategy to periodically evaluate their scientific and ethical status.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Morally relevant features warranting ethical oversight in human stem cell-based embryo models
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 08 April 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01881-4 This Perspective presents a set of attributes by which to evaluate human stem cell-based embryo models that not only include morally relevant embryo features but also take into account proposed use of the model and regulatory considerations.

Nature Cell Biology: Aberrant amino acid-sensing promotes immunotherapy resistance via the inflammatory cytokine–ZBTB5–mTORC1 axis
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 03 April 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01926-8 Xiang, Wang, Tian et al. report that during nutrient insufficiency, inflammatory cytokines promote a ZBTB5-mediated mechanism to activate mTORC1 signalling, thereby enhancing amino acid uptake in tumour cells and restricting antitumour immune response.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Mosaic gastruloids reveal a temporal restriction for developmental cell competition
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 01 April 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01923-x Frenster et al. utilize mosaic mouse gastruloids as a model of cell fitness and competition, identifying a temporal window between primed pluripotency and early gastrulation during which cell competition occurs in mammalian embryogenesis.
